compound.name: ursolic acid
compound.one_liner: Waxy pentacyclic triterpene acid in sage, rosemary and lemon balm leaves.

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Melissa officinalis L., folium. EMA/HMPC/196746/2012 (14 May 2013). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-melissa-officinalis-l-folium_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: URSOLIC-ACID Plant, no value. EMA: 'Triterpenes including ursolic and oleanolic acids' (no amount).

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Salvia officinalis L., folium and Salvia officinalis L., aetheroleum, Rev. 1. EMA/HMPC/150801/2015 (20 Sep 2016). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-salvia-officinalis-l-folium-and-salvia-officinalis-l-aetheroleum-revision-1_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: Leaf 1255-1300 ppm; Stem max 200 ppm. LOTUS ursolic acid (LTS0250838) lists Salvia officinalis (ref 10.1016/S0378-8741(00)00396-2 as decoded). | Basis as recorded: dried leaf (as given in EMA report)

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Rosmarinus officinalis L., aetheroleum and Rosmarinus officinalis L., folium, Rev. 1. EMA/HMPC/681037/2021 (29 May 2024). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/final-assessment-report-rosmarinus-officinalis-l-aetheroleum-rosmarinus-officinalis-l-folium-revision-1_en.pdf
occurrences.note: EMA names ursolic acid among rosemary leaf constituents (no amount). Database record not confirmed: the Duke CSV response was truncated before 'U', KNApSAcK Rosmarinus list has no ursolic acid, LOTUS visible JSON did not show Rosmarinus (truncated).

compound.teaching_note: A leaf-surface triterpene, chemically unlike the volatile oil; the oregano row was dropped because no source confirmed it.
gaps: Oregano occurrence dropped (not verified); TODO(author) on the oregano page.
Rosemary row rests on the EMA report only (no database record).
Pharmacology, absorption and safety not researched.
No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
